title: 900 Individual Portrait Images.. Is this possible and with what?
author: BoxingWorldSimulator
selftext:
I am looking for a bit of advice or even clarification that its not possible.

Essentially id like to have AI generate me 900 images (at least) of a portrait of a boxers face/stance. Each of them to be individual and read from a file that will show their Nationality/Age and use that to generate.

The image needs to be realistic but computer game realistic (if that makes sense) and just give me a back a mix of poses as well as the unique face for each person.

I have tried ChatGPT to do this and it does to an extent, I can get it to maybe give me 15, before then it starts to re-use the same faces, just changes hair or smile etc.

Any advice would be appreciated as to where to go with this?

comments.author: AustinMHowe
comments.body:
Without a lot of context on exacts I’ll share some learnings:  
\- Don’t use ambiguous prompts with image models. “Give me this image with 15 unique expressions”  
\- Do work with a text based model to make explicit expressions first and align the prompts for the image models  
\- Do use the batch api. Cuts the cost in half and takes longer but with 900 you’ll have to review this likely fine. You can make one batch per boxer to make it easier to review  
\- I would personally create an initial version of the boxer manually in the style you want and use it for a reference image with the prompt.

comments.author: Minute-Soil-674
comments.body: Download a open-source model from civitai or huggingface and get chatgpt to help you set up a comfy UI workflow to run it on your own GPU. Run 900 different seeds (again, chatgpt can organize for you) and it should be different everytime. Depending on your gpu will take 1-3 nights

comments.author: asd849849494984984
comments.body:
Depending on what size you want the portraits to be you can generate more in a single image, by having it split up, or at least generate the face and stance in the same image. And with that many unique faces  you have no other option than being very specific about the features you want.

And I hate to be the guy, but I have to question why you would need so many. Maybe just generate a few to test the game, and generate the rest at the end, if you really think that's necessary.

You could also overlay spites in game to create characters based on mixing features, kind of like the crusader kings 2 character creator.

comments.author: forgetscode
comments.body: you need to use a set of references then build a skill and should use codex for this. having your first good gens as the reference set to refer to would work. your skill should cover the deviations your seeing. so you have to monitor it and develop strategies for where things go wrong. this should be very doable.

comments.author: Key-Helicopter4051
comments.body: For 900 images, I would look at a batch image workflow rather than trying to generate them one at a time. You will still need a good way to keep each character’s face and details consistent. Mage Space is worth checking for larger batch-style generation and different models. The bigger challenge will be the seed and prompt setup, especially if every boxer needs a genuinely different face. I would test it with 50–100 characters first and lock down the workflow before scaling to all 900. That should make it easier to avoid getting the same faces with only small changes.

comments.author: beikbeikbeik
comments.body:
Why don’t you try to make it a procedural generation by splitting body type, pose, skin color, eye/nose/mouth type, etc…?

If you try use GenAI for it, you will need to deal with two issues:  
\- The style will drift after a few images. You need to start a fresh session for the previous generations not influence the new ones  
\- You can feed a style reference image in the start of every session. It will unfortunately “lock down” the possibilities and all images will kind of look too similar after a while
